actions.action: Retry only attachments that need attention
actions.mechanism: Track each file separately; accepted receipts stay attached while failed files offer explicit recovery choices.
actions.implementation: Show uploading, accepted, failed, or unconfirmed status per row. Retry failed rows only; allow removal or replacement. Never automatically retry unconfirmed uploads.
actions.check: Force two of five uploads to fail. Retry them and verify the three accepted files generate no additional upload requests.
actions.risk: Lost responses require receipt reconciliation; otherwise acceptance remains unconfirmed.

actions.action: Explain recovery when the tab reopens
actions.mechanism: Restore accepted attachments from unexpired receipts, while clearly distinguishing them from files whose browser selection was lost.
actions.implementation: Persist only opaque receipt identifiers for 24 hours. Resolve them server-side on reopening; explain unavailable receipts and request missing file selections again.
actions.check: Close after partial acceptance, then reopen. Accepted attachments remain available without reupload; missing selections require reselection. Repeat with expired receipts.
actions.risk: Without receipts, recovery cannot promise access to previously accepted files.

actions.action: Require review of the exact final list
actions.mechanism: Separate attachment recovery from case submission so partial batches cannot silently become final cases.
actions.implementation: Present a receipt-backed review list capped at five files. Require explicit confirmation; invalidate it after edits and disable repeated submission while pending.
actions.check: Remove or replace an attachment after review: submission must require renewed confirmation. Double-click submit: only one request leaves the page.
actions.risk: Client-side locking cannot prevent duplicates after an ambiguous submission response.
